messages:
Jordan: hey y'all, jordan here — first week, trying to run the example pipeline but the docker publish step fails with a weird auth error. not sure if i messed up the token or the pipeline secret scope. who should i ping?

Buildkite Bot: build #3 failed: step `publish-image` (exit 1)
```
> Pushing to ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox:pr-2
> denied: requested access to the resource is denied
> error: failed to push some refs to 'ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox'
```

Jordan: pipeline env shows GHCR_PAT set in the project settings. i copied the token from my GitHub > developer settings. i included packages scope when I created it.

Riya: welcome! :wave: two quick possibilities: (1) token missing org SSO authorization, (2) Buildkite job isn't actually picking up the secret because of pipeline-level masking/visibility or the agent's docker config path. did you create the PAT from an account that's in the org and approve SSO?

Jordan: hmm i think i clicked through SSO during onboarding but not 100% sure. how would i confirm?

Alex: another gotcha — we sometimes use a custom docker config dir in our pipeline to share creds across steps: `DOCKER_CONFIG=/root/.docker-ci`. if your login step writes to a different config path than the publish step reads from, publish will fail with denied even if token works. can you paste the `publish-image` step snippet?

Jordan: sure, it's here:
```
steps:
  - label: ":docker: build + publish"
    commands:
      - docker build -t $IMAGE:$BUILDKITE_COMMIT .
      - echo "$GHCR_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u $GITHUB_USER --password-stdin
      - docker push $IMAGE:$BUILDKITE_COMMIT
    env:
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox
      DOCKER_CONFIG: /root/.docker-ci
```

Riya: ah ok — i see the env var DOCKER_CONFIG is set, but the login command as written writes to the default docker config (~/.docker) unless you set `DOCKER_CONFIG` in the same command environment. CI steps run in a shell so the env should apply, but if Buildkite runs the login in a different plugin container or step stage it might not. also masked secrets sometimes get truncated if the secret includes newlines or was accidentally wrapped.

Jordan: i did copy the token and it looked right. how can i quickly validate the token locally and also confirm SSO?

Alex: locally run:
```
echo "$CANDIDATE_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u <your-gh-username> --password-stdin
docker push ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox:canary-test
```
for SSO check: visit https://github.com/organizations/redwood-inference/settings/profile and ensure your account shows SAML/SSO approved, or run `gh auth status` and check if `User: <you> (SSO)` appears.

Jordan: ran the docker login locally and it worked, pushed my test image. so token + packages scopes are fine. weird.

Riya: ok that narrows it. can you paste the raw buildkite step log around the login? sometimes the pipeline uses a Docker plugin and runs the `docker login` in a helper container that doesn't share the DOCKER_CONFIG dir with the main step.

Buildkite Bot: uploading raw build log...

Jordan: log excerpt:
```
+++ Building image
+++ echo "[secure]"
+++ docker login ghcr.io -u jordan --password-stdin
Login Succeeded
+++ docker push ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox:pr-2
denied: requested access to the resource is denied
```

Alex: interesting — the login prints `Login Succeeded` but the push is denied. that strongly suggests the login credentials are being written to a different config than the docker client doing the push, or the push is happening with a different user context (e.g., a different agent container). check if the pipeline uses `plugins: docker#v#` or runs multiple parallel agents.

Riya: also confirm the image name is spelled correctly and that the repo exists under the org. if the repo is a personal sandbox and our org doesn't own the repo name, GHCR may deny pushes. `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox` must be an image name you're allowed to push to.

Jordan: it's a repo in the org: `redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox`. Buildkite project is tied to the forked repo though (my PR). could that cause a token permission mismatch?

Alex: yes — if Buildkite runs the pipeline from the forked repo context, the org app might not be installed on the fork, and the PAT used might be your personal account which needs explicit package permission for org repos and SSO approval. Could be a combination.

Riya: quick next steps: (1) re-run the build but add an explicit `docker login` line that sets DOCKER_CONFIG inline: `DOCKER_CONFIG=/root/.docker-ci echo "$GHCR_PAT" | docker login ghcr.io -u $GITHUB_USER --password-stdin`; (2) if that fails, switch the pipeline to use the org GitHub App token (ping infra) or have infra temporarily add your user to `ci-testers` team so the app covers your fork builds.

Jordan: ok i'll try the inline DOCKER_CONFIG trick and re-run.

Jordan: requeued build with inline DOCKER_CONFIG.

Buildkite Bot: build #4 started - step `publish-image`

Buildkite Bot: build #4 succeeded :tada: - image pushed to ghcr.io/redwood-inference/jordan-sandbox:pr-2

Jordan: woohoo, that fixed it. thanks y'all. i'll add a note to my onboarding doc: "If using DOCKER_CONFIG make sure login and push use the same config path; forks + org app mismatch can be subtle." cc @Riya @Alex for the quick walkthrough later. :smile:
